Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an administrator user in the EduCentral application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Admin entity.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the admin account was created.

lastLogin.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the admin logged in.

Student.title: Student
Student.description: Represents a student user in the EduCentral application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Student entity.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth of the student.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the student account was created.

lastLogin.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the student logged in.

Lecturer.title: Lecturer
Lecturer.description: Represents a lecturer user in the EduCentral application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Lecturer entity.

hireDate.description: Date when the lecturer was hired.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the lecturer account was created.

lastLogin.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the lecturer logged in.

Course.title: Course
Course.description: Represents a course offered in the EduCentral application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Course entity.

credits.description: Number of credits the course is worth.

Enrollment.title: Enrollment
Enrollment.description: Represents a student's enrollment in a course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Enrollment entity.

enrollmentDate.description: Date when the student enrolled in the course.

grade.description: The grade the student received in the course.

Attendance.title: Attendance
Attendance.description: Represents a student's attendance record for a specific course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Attendance entity.

isPresent.description: Indicates whether the student was present or absent.

Payment.title: Payment
Payment.description: Represents a payment made by a student.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Payment entity.

paymentDate.description: Date when the payment was made.

paymentMethod.description: Method used for the payment (e.g., credit card, bank transfer).

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a notification sent to a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Notification entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who received the notification. Can be Admin, Student, or Lecturer.

timestamp.description: Timestamp indicating when the notification was sent.

isRead.description: Indicates whether the notification has been read.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support EduCentral's role-based access control and data management features, focusing on security, scalability, and ease of debugging. The structure uses path-based ownership for private user data and membership maps for collaborative data. Authorization independence is achieved through denormalization.  All collections are designed to have a homogeneous security posture. This design prioritizes the core design principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters).

**Authorization Independence & Denormalization:**

*   For entities nested under users (e.g., Payments, Attendance), the `studentId` field acts as the owner and is present in every document, enabling rules to validate ownership without `get()` calls.
*   The Course documents include `lecturerId` to denote ownership and allow lecturers to manage their courses. Enrollments do not need to denormalize additional fields given they are subcollections of both Students and Courses.
*   Notifications are created to `/notifications/{notificationId}` and will require rules to allow admins to create and users to view notifications which target their user ID.

**Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**

*   Each top-level collection (e.g., `/admins`, `/students`, `/lecturers`, `/courses`, `/notifications`) contains documents of the same type and security requirements.

**Access Modeling:**

*   **Private Data:** User profiles (`/admins/{adminId}`, `/students/{studentId}`, `/lecturers/{lecturerId}`) use path-based ownership.
*   **Collaborative Data:** While not explicitly collaborative in the initial schema, if Courses were to become collaborative (e.g., multiple lecturers), a `members` map could be added to the `Course` entity and denormalized to subcollections if necessary.
*   **Global Roles (DBAC):** The existence of a document in `/admins/{adminId}` implicitly grants admin privileges. Rules can check for the existence of this document to authorize admin-only operations.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

*   The data structure enables secure `list` operations. For example, a lecturer can securely list courses they own (where `course.lecturerId == request.auth.uid`). A student can list their own enrollments (where `enrollment.studentId == request.auth.uid`).

**Invariants:**

*   Timestamps (`createdAt`, `enrollmentDate`, `paymentDate`, `timestamp`) can be enforced via rules to ensure data integrity.

This structure avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies by denormalizing authorization context (Strategy A), ensures homogeneous security postures within collections (Strategy B), and employs consistent access modeling patterns (Strategy C). It also promotes data clarity and predictability through explicit state modeling and semantic naming conventions (Strategy D).
